mission.display_title: Name response and explanatory variables with modelling intent
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to make response vs explanatory naming a deliberate modelling move — so you enter linear regression with a clear outcome variable and predictors, without pretending simple/multiple model forms (4.1.2) are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to discriminate response from explanatory variables on an actuarial data sketch and refuse treating 'all columns are predictors' as modelling.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from hypothesis-testing closure (3.3) to lawful response/explanatory roles at the Continuity Front join into Section 4.
mission.concept_focus: Data sketch → name Y → name X's → refuse column-soup modelling → refuse simple/multiple swallow.
mission.prior_bridge: Campaign Mu closed hypothesis testing and goodness of fit (3.3) with Revision. Today opens Continuity Front join at Topic 4.1 LO 4.1.1 — the next official syllabus topic after 3.3. Trust Front CS1-003 already holds LIVE 4.1 inventory independently; Nu is the Continuity Front native Pilot Arc.
mission.why_now: 4.1.1 is the lawful Continuity Front join after Mu. Closing it prevents a cliff at regression roles while keeping simple/multiple models as day two.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for variable roles — not Topic Complete for 4.1.2.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Nu Day 1 because CE-001 / EP-001 Continuity Front names 4.1 as the handoff from Mu after Chapter 3 CF Missing closes.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name one response and at least one explanatory variable for a stated scenario.
Justify each role in one sentence.
Refuse one 'every column is a predictor' claim.
task_descriptions: Sketch response vs explanatory roles before CMP.
Complete Guided Reading through CMP treatment of Syllabus 4.1.1.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What is a response variable? (2) What is an explanatory variable? (3) Give one actuarial-flavoured pair (Y, X). (4) Name one reason simple vs multiple models are not today's LO.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Response is the outcome modelled; explanatory variables are the predictors. Example: claim severity (Y) vs age and sum insured (X's). Simple/multiple model forms are tomorrow's LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A colleague says 'I listed every column as a predictor, so I finished today's LO.' Refuse in one sentence and restate what today's LO requires.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse: column-soup is not modelling. Today requires deliberate response vs explanatory naming with justification.
